the olfactory nerve fibers excite the mitral cells monosynaptically, and that the mitral cells are inhibited by the interneurons in the olfactory bulbs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the properties of the synaptic inputs to mitral cells in the olfactory bulbs of the rabbit.
the functional organization of the olfactory bulb, with particular emphasis on the role of glomeruli in processing information.
the synaptic organization of the olfactory bulb, and with the properties of the olfactory nerve fibres.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the olfactory nerve volly elicits a synaptic excitation in mitral and tufts cells.
the olfactory nerve fibres excite both mitral and tufts cells, with the former being more readily excitable.
olfactory nerve volles excite and inhibit the output cells of the olfactory bulb through interneuronal pathways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the olfactory nerve volley excites the mitral and tufts cell dendrites directly in the glomerular region of the bulb, but that it also excites and inhibits the cell bodies through interneurons.

The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that the olfactory nerve can directly activate mitral and tufter cells.
the olfactory bulb is not just a relay station for information from the nose to the brain.
